findings.title: Ruin is assigned a governed closure
findings.claim: The appointment clause makes destruction a governed transition into a specified ruin-state: wrongdoing remains the stated cause, while the end is assigned rather than impulsively imposed.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier جَعَلْنَا at 18:59:6:2 supplies the setting operation; the separate مَّوْعِدًا at 18:59:8:1 and the supplied parallels at 16:61, 22:48, 15:5, and 18:98 return through that operation as evidence of delay, fixed term, and promised closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The interval between wrongdoing and ruin becomes legible as meaningful governance: reprieve and consequence can occupy the same sentence without turning the destruction into arbitrary disappearance.
findings.containment: This retains the focus's completed divine destruction and its wrongdoing clause. It does not read جَعَلَ as creation, naming, or beginning an action, and it does not make time itself the destroying agent.

epistemic.reason: A citable trusted publication explicitly anchors the branch to the focus carrier, and strong or medium packet connections independently join wrongdoing, respite, fixed terms, and the later same-surah promised end.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The separate appointment noun and the supplied delayed-term and promised-end relations provide the independent boundary that activates the setting-state branch.
branch_activations.activation: The setting operation contacts the focus's destruction noun and appointed term, changing the reading from bare ruin to ruin placed within a governed endpoint.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Destruction is presented as an assigned closure after wrongdoing, with the interval before it carrying the sense of measured governance.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation does not claim creation, naming, or an action-starting construction, and it does not replace the primary causal reading.

findings.title: Ruin is a reached boundary
findings.claim: The paired destruction forms can make the towns' end perceptible as a reached and appointed boundary: the communities are actually brought to ruin, while their ruin is also named as an endpoint rather than an undirected vanishing.
findings.mechanism: أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ at 18:59:3:1 carries caused extinction and مَهْلِكِهِمْ at 18:59:7:2 names the destruction event; the separate appointment at 18:59:8:1 and the fixed-term connections at 15:4, 15:5, and 16:61 supply the independent terminal relation. The trusted candidate support also supplies the journey-boundary image for the weaker place facet.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence holds consequence and location together: destruction is not a random erasure, but an end reached under a stated appointment, with the ruin image remaining materially present.
findings.containment: The B001 activations keep both the core loss result and its transitive realization. B006 is an analogical, form-distant resonance only; it does not claim that the focus noun literally denotes a wilderness, abyss, journey, or that time itself destroys.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support explicitly nominates both branches, while the core B001 relation is strongly connected to fixed decrees; the B006 place image remains weak and analogical, and packet connection rows do not supply target morphology.

findings.title: A promised end need not signal failed governance
findings.claim: The focus appointment can be read beside the later barrier's promised collapse as a scheduled end that fulfills an established order, so an arrangement's eventual removal need not imply that its protection or governance failed.
findings.mechanism: The focus word مَّوْعِدًا carries the appointment; the exact same-surah connection to 18:98 supplies a later promise whose fulfillment removes the barrier, returning the wider event through the focus's appointed-end relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The end of the towns' protected interval becomes compatible with purposeful governance: delay and eventual closure belong to one ordered movement.
findings.containment: This is a qualified same-surah analogy, not a claim that the focus towns are the barrier or that every appointment has the same form. The primary wrongdoing-and-destruction relation remains recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective support is legacy_unbound and non-citable, while the packet supplies a medium same-surah connection to 18:98 that makes the endpoint analogy concrete.

findings.title: The boundary can be passed without correction
findings.claim: The later travel retrospective gives the destruction node an exploratory overshoot image: a boundary can be passed while correction is still possible, and ruin becomes the uncorrected crossing rather than arbitrary disappearance.
findings.mechanism: The focus destruction noun مَهْلِكِهِمْ and appointment noun مَّوْعِدًا provide the carrier pair; the supplied 18:60–62 retrospective supplies the wider traveler-and-boundary trigger and returns its missed-correction image to those focus words.
findings.reader_payoff: The appointed end becomes perceptible as a boundary with a possible missed response, adding consequence and direction to the bare image of ruin.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory, form-distant analogy from a legacy_unbound retrospective. The focus lexeme is not being redefined as travel, fatigue, or a literal spatial overshoot, and the primary historical destruction remains intact.
